title: scopingreview
text:
PPADEM Code & Packages


An automated, user-friendly R pipeline for conducting systematic and scoping literature reviews across Elsevier Scopus and OpenAlex bibliographic databases.

title: scopingreview
text:
🎯 What This Tool Does
This pipeline automates the labor-intensive initial stages of a systematic literature review:

Constructs Boolean API Queries: Combines your thematic search keywords and geographic filters using precise boolean logic across both Scopus and OpenAlex, supporting single-category (OR / AND) or multi-block (multi) search modes.
Queries Scopus & OpenAlex: Programmatically retrieves academic publications, handling pagination and rate limits automatically.
Harmonizes Metadata: Standardizes schemas across both databases into a single clean format.
Performs 2-Stage Deduplication: Merges duplicate papers across databases using exact DOI matching and fuzzy title string matching.
Flags Curated Target Journals: Automatically checks each paper’s journal against a reference list of 137 top Political Science, Administrative, and Area/African Studies journals and flags them (Y / N) in a dedicated column.
Exports Customizable Datasets: Saves structured CSV datasets directly to root or to custom subfolder paths specified in output_filename.

title: scopingreview
text:
🔍 How the Search Logic Works
Understanding how your search parameters are built into API queries:

1. Topic Keywords (OR, AND, or multi Logic)
Keywords grouped inside each topic category in SEARCH_TOPICS are joined together using the topic_operator setting:

OR Mode (default): ("political party" OR "party organization" OR "party decline")
AND Mode: ("political party" AND "party organization" AND "party decline")
MULTI Mode: Combines multiple concept blocks (e.g. BLOCK 1 AND BLOCK 2 AND … AND BLOCK N), where terms inside each block are separated by OR: ((Block 1 terms separated by OR) AND (Block 2 terms separated by OR)) AND (GEO terms separated by OR)



2. Geographic Terms (OR Logic, Optional)
Geographic terms in GEO_TERMS are optional. When provided, they are joined together with OR operators:

("Africa" OR "Sub-Saharan Africa" OR "West Africa")

If geo_terms = NULL or omitted, no geographic filter is applied, allowing for a general/global broad search.


3. Combining Topics & Geography (AND Logic)
When geo_terms are provided, the pipeline joins the topic group and the geographic group together using an AND operator. When geo_terms is NULL, only the topic query and publication year filter are applied:
Final Query with Geography = (Topic Keywords [OR/AND]) AND (Geographic Terms [OR]) AND PUBYEAR >= START_YEAR
Final Query without Geography = (Topic Keywords [OR/AND]) AND PUBYEAR >= START_YEAR

title: scopingreview
text:
⚙️ Quick Start Guide

1. Installation
Install the package directly from GitHub (R version 4.1+ recommended). Its dependencies (rscopus, openalexR, dplyr, etc.) are installed automatically:
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("PPADEM/scopingreview")
Then load it with:
library(scopingreview)


2. API Key Setup
Store your API keys in your user R environment file (~/.Renviron). This allows R to automatically authenticate your queries without hardcoding keys in your script:
Add the following lines to ~/.Renviron:
OPENALEX_KEY="your_openalex_api_key"
ELSEVIER_SCOPUS_KEY="your_scopus_api_key"

title: scopingreview
section: 🛠️ Customizing Output File Locations & Search Modes
text:
🛠️ Customizing Output File Locations & Search Modes
By default, files are saved in your current working directory. If a subfolder path is included in output_filename, the directory is created automatically:
library(scopingreview)

# Run 1: General Broad Search (OR mode)
general_data <- run_scoping_review(
  search_topics   = list(party = c("political party", "party decline")),
  geo_terms       = c("Africa", "Sub-Saharan Africa"),
  start_year      = 2020,
  topic_operator  = "OR",
  output_filename = "general_search.csv"
)

# Run 2: Multi-Block Search (BLOCK 1 AND BLOCK 2 AND GEO)
multi_data <- run_scoping_review(
  search_topics   = list(
    parties = c("political party", "party organization"),
    communication = c("communication", "meeting", "social media")
  ),
  geo_terms       = c("Africa", "Sub-Saharan Africa"),
  start_year      = 2020,
  topic_operator  = "multi",
  output_filename = "outputs/multi_block_search.csv"
)

Long searches and rate limits
OpenAlex rejects queries over 1,500 characters. In "multi" mode, run_scoping_review() automatically splits long term lists (max_query_chars = 1400 by default; NULL disables it), runs every combination, and merges and deduplicates the results. Large searches therefore become many API calls: preview them with chunk_search_topics(). OpenAlex pages are fetched one at a time (about 1 second each, capped at 50 pages / 10,000 records per query), so set OPENALEX_KEY to avoid shared rate limits.

title: scopingreview
text:
🚀 Example Script
A complete example script with three different search runs is included with the package. Copy it to your working directory to use as a starting point:
file.copy(
  system.file("examples", "api_pipeline_example.R", package = "scopingreview"),
  "api_pipeline_example.R"
)
Or view it on GitHub at inst/examples/api_pipeline_example.R.
Help pages are available for each exported function, e.g. ?run_scoping_review.

text:
📊 Output File Schema
Outputs are exported to the location specified in output_filename:








Column Name
Description
Example




database
Provenance database source(s)
Scopus; OpenAlex


query_category
Thematic search category or multi-block combination
party_linkages or party_block & communication_block


search_query
Exact Boolean API search query string executed for this record
("political party" OR "party decline") AND ("Africa" OR ...)


search_date
Date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the search pipeline was executed
2026-08-24


scopus_id
Scopus record identifier
2-s2.0-85123456789


openalex_id
OpenAlex work URI
https://openalex.org/W4323539164


title
Article title
Parties, Political Finance, and Representation


journal
Source journal / publication name
Journal of Modern African Studies


publication_year
Year of publication
2023


doi
Standardized DOI
10.1017/s0022278x2300001


citations
Highest reported citation count
14


abstract
Full article text abstract
This article examines...


authors
Semicolon-separated list of author names
Smith, J.; Kwame, A.


target_journal
Flag (Y/N) indicating if journal matches curated political science/administrative/African studies list
Y

title: scopingreview (development)
text:
fetch_openalex_data() and run_scoping_review() gain openalex_scope, defaulting to "title_abstract". OpenAlex is now queried with the title_and_abstract.search filter, which matches the scope of Scopus’s TITLE-ABS-KEY. Previously OpenAlex used search=, which also matches full text and stems terms. That returned far more records than Scopus, mostly irrelevant ones (9 vs 16,895 in one run), and made heavy queries slow. openalex_scope = "fulltext" restores the old behaviour. This changes which records a review finds. Results from earlier versions are not comparable.
OpenAlex search_query values are prefixed with the parameter used (title_and_abstract.search: or search:), so the CSV shows how each record was found.
Commas in search terms are replaced with spaces in title-and-abstract mode, because OpenAlex uses commas to separate filters.
The end-of-run summary warns when one database returns more than 100 times as many records as the other.





run_scoping_review() gains max_query_chars (default 1400). In "multi" mode, term lists (and geographic terms) are split until every query fits OpenAlex’s 1,500-character limit; all combinations are run, merged and deduplicated once. New exported chunk_search_topics() previews the split.
The final banner now reports records and failed requests per database, and warns instead of reporting success when a database contributes nothing.





OpenAlex pages are fetched one at a time (1.1 s apart, capped at 50 pages), stopping on a short or empty page.
Only the failed page is retried (5 attempts, 2/5/10 s back-off); “Rate limit exceeded” is treated as retryable, and an empty result with a warning is treated as a failure.
Errors are no longer silently swallowed; empty pages are no longer retried; api_key is passed only when OPENALEX_KEY is set, with a message otherwise.
OpenAlex timeouts and other transient network errors (DNS, connection resets, SSL, empty replies) are now retried, with a 120 s request timeout (was 30 s) and a 5/10/20/30/60 s back-off. Previously a timeout silently cut a query short.
A page that cannot be fetched is no longer mistaken for the end of results: paging stops with a warning that the query is incomplete, keeping the pages already retrieved.
openalexR’s per-page progress messages are suppressed.
Added testthat tests for query splitting and retry logic.

title: scopingreview (development)
text:
Bug Fixes & API Resilience

OpenAlex compatibility: Fixed a critical failure where upstream schema changes in OpenAlex (adding doi inside primary_location) caused openalexR (<= 3.1.1) to crash with Column name 'doi' must not be duplicated. Queries now fetch via output = "list", sanitize nested duplicate fields, and convert safely via oa2df().
Scopus view authorization: Added scopus_view parameter (defaulting to "STANDARD") to fetch_scopus_data() and run_scoping_review(). If "COMPLETE" view is requested with an API key lacking institutional entitlement, the pipeline now logs an informative message and falls back gracefully to "STANDARD" instead of failing with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
OpenAlex empty search handling: Genuinely empty search results (signaled by "No records found!") no longer trigger multiple redundant backoff retry sleep cycles.

title: scopingreview (development)
text:
Packaging & Build Improvements

Portability & R CMD check: Added ^docs$ and ^_extensions$ to .Rbuildignore so Quarto website assets and presentation extensions do not cause file path length or non-portable name warnings during package builds.
Transitive deduplication: Refined Stage 2 fuzzy title deduplication to use union-find with path compression for consistent transitive grouping.
